clinical_category: Liver transplant assessment - current MELD calculator inputs
blueprint_topic: Interpretation of objective laboratory and clinical data used in transplant urgency scoring
stem: A nurse is reviewing the current OPTN MELD calculation for an adult liver-transplant candidate. Which set of data accurately reflects the current calculator inputs?

options.A: Bilirubin, creatinine, INR, sodium, albumin, candidate age at listing, and sex for the adult MELD calculation.
options.B: Bilirubin, creatinine, and INR only; sodium, albumin, age, and sex are not used in the current calculation.
options.C: Ascites grade, encephalopathy grade, albumin, bilirubin, and prothrombin time as a direct copy of the Child-Pugh score.
options.D: Serum ammonia alone because the current MELD system uses one laboratory value to determine transplant urgency.

rationale: A is correct. The current HRSA/OPTN MELD calculator, updated effective July 13, 2023 and reviewed in December 2025, lists serum creatinine, bilirubin, INR, serum sodium, albumin, candidate age at listing, and sex for purposes of adult MELD calculation among its inputs. B describes an older, incomplete MELD formulation and omits current inputs. C incorrectly substitutes Child-Pugh components; the current MELD calculator does not use ascites or encephalopathy grade as direct formula inputs. D is incorrect because ammonia is not the sole or defining MELD input. The final item replaces the outdated 'MELD-Na' wording and secondary calculator source with the current official OPTN/HRSA calculator and avoids asking the nurse to memorize formula coefficients.
educational_objective: Identify the current official OPTN MELD calculator inputs and distinguish them from older MELD/MELD-Na descriptions and Child-Pugh components.
